halfLife.notes: Active metabolite of venlafaxine (O-desmethylvenlafaxine). Predictable pharmacokinetics — less CYP2D6 variability than venlafaxine. Once-daily dosing. Steady state in ~4-5 days. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

activeMetabolite.notes: Desvenlafaxine IS the active metabolite of venlafaxine. No further active metabolites of clinical significance.

cypInteractions.switchingRelevance: Unlike venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine is not significantly metabolised by CYP2D6 — plasma levels are less variable across CYP2D6 phenotypes. Moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor — may raise levels of co-prescribed CYP2D6 substrates (risperidone, haloperidol). No washout advantage over venlafaxine for switching purposes. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

maoiWashout.notes: Same MAOI washout rules as venlafaxine — 14 days off desvenlafaxine before starting any MAOI; 14 days off any MAOI before starting desvenlafaxine. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

discontinuationSyndromeRisk.notes: Similar discontinuation syndrome to venlafaxine — dizziness, nausea, 'brain zaps', sweating on abrupt cessation. Taper over at least 2 weeks; consider hyperbolic taper for long-term users. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

formulationNotes: Extended-release tablets — do NOT crush, cut or chew. Swallow whole. 50 mg/day is the recommended effective dose for most patients; 100 mg/day offers no clear additional efficacy but higher side-effect burden. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
specialConsiderations: Therapeutic equivalency to venlafaxine is not direct — dose conversion is approximate. Venlafaxine 75 mg ≈ desvenlafaxine 50 mg is a common reference.
CYP2D6 inhibition (moderate) — monitor risperidone, TCAs, opioids metabolised by CYP2D6.
Avoid in severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) — dose adjustment required.
